current_state_summary.primary_concern: Close the Accord sale before the market absorbs the RoboRide launch and used car values soften further. Validate the RoboRide thesis with a real trip, not just a model.

threat_assessment.immediate: No immediate threat. RoboRide launching today is the event I modeled. The only real urgency is that every day the Accord sits unsold is a day my first-mover price premium erodes. Two serious buyers are in the pipeline. One of them needs to sign this week.
threat_assessment.horizon_2mo: Transport cost structure will be fully resolved — Accord gone, RoboRide + occasional Zipcar or rental in place, monthly commuting spend drops from ~$847 (car ownership share) to roughly $390-450. Savings get a ~$18,800 one-time injection. The Millfield economy will start showing more visible stress as the employment ripple from auto sector contraction reaches service businesses. My job is not at risk but my employer's clients and the broader spending environment will tighten.
threat_assessment.horizon_6mo: Tech employment remains strong. If RoboRide Phase 2 expands coverage into residential areas, the car-light model becomes car-free for me. The community around me may be hurting — Lisa Freeman's center and the small business corridor will feel the contraction. There may be a meaningful role for me as a tech-skilled resident who isn't in crisis and can contribute something.

actions.description: Close the Accord sale. Contact both serious buyers today — email or text within the hour — to confirm test drive slots this week. Frame it as availability, not pressure. Be prepared to accept $18,800 on the spot if either buyer makes a cash offer or comes pre-financed. Do not let either appointment slip to next week. If buyer one falls through, immediately move buyer two into the primary slot the same day.
actions.rationale: RoboRide launched this morning at $0.18/mile. That is the inflection point I identified when I listed the car. The market has now received the same signal I was acting on in advance. Every motivated buyer in Millfield who was undecided about their own car situation now has a concrete alternative — which means the pool of people who will buy a used car for full private-party value is shrinking in real time. Closing at $18,800 today is worth more than $17,200 in six weeks. The $600 concession from list price has a positive IRR measured in days, not years. The sale closes this tick.
actions.timeline: This week. Both test drives within 48 hours. Accept any offer at or above $18,800 immediately. Floor is $18,500 but I am not advertising the floor.
actions.expected_outcome: Accord sells for $18,800. Proceeds deposited. Savings jump from $105,288 to approximately $124,088 after accounting for monthly surplus. Monthly expenses drop by the car ownership share — insurance, maintenance reserve, depreciation — estimated $580/month freed. Transport line item shifts from ~$847 blended to approximately $390-430 on RoboRide + occasional rental.

actions.description: Download the RoboRide app today. Take one real trip this week — commute direction, not a test loop around the block. Log actual wait time, actual ride time, actual fare, and a qualitative score on the experience: comfort, reliability, ability to work during the ride. Compare against the model.
actions.rationale: I have been analyzing this service on a spreadsheet for three ticks. The numbers justify the thesis. But a spreadsheet is not a product review, and I am about to restructure my entire commute around this service. One real data point is worth more than ten projected ones. If the 15-minute stated wait time is actually 22 minutes in Millfield conditions, I need to know that now, not after the car is sold — though the car is selling regardless. The goal is to validate the experience layer, not the financial layer. I already know the financial case closes.
actions.timeline: App download today. First trip within the next 5 days. Log results immediately after the ride while the data is fresh.
actions.expected_outcome: Either RoboRide performs close to spec — in which case my confidence in the model goes from 0.85 to 0.95 — or I surface a gap (wait time, coverage edge, ride quality) that I need to account for in the longer-term plan. Either outcome is useful. The thesis survives both.

actions.description: Map my specific commute pattern against the RoboRide + train + Zipcar combination. Identify the two or three edge cases — late meetings, weekend trips out of coverage, the occasional client site visit outside city limits — and price a realistic monthly transport budget for each scenario. Build the post-car mobility stack explicitly, not as an abstraction.
actions.rationale: Going car-light is not the same as going car-free, and I should not conflate them. My commute pattern is 45 minutes each way on workdays, but there are maybe four to six trips per month that fall outside the RoboRide coverage zone or timing window. Zipcar covers those at roughly $14-18/hour. I need to know whether my actual mobility needs fit in $420/month or $580/month — that is the number I will be living with, and I want it modeled against reality, not the average case.
actions.timeline: This week. One evening, two hours, spreadsheet update. No action required from anyone else.
actions.expected_outcome: A clean post-car monthly transport budget with a realistic range (low/mid/high scenarios). This becomes my baseline for evaluating whether to keep a Zipcar membership, whether to push for a corporate transport allowance from my employer, and whether RoboRide Phase 2 coverage expansion changes the calculus.

actions.description: Identify one concrete way to contribute to the Millfield community response to this disruption. Specific candidates: reach out to Lisa Freeman's community center about volunteer tech skills (website, database, digital literacy classes), or offer informal mentorship to two or three displaced auto-sector workers who might have aptitude for tech-adjacent roles. Do not over-commit. One thing, done well.
actions.rationale: I am not affected by this disruption in the way most of Millfield is. My job is secure, my finances are healthy, and I saw this coming early enough to act. That position carries some obligation — not guilt, but the practical fact that I have skills and bandwidth that are scarce right now in this community. The spending index is at 76 and falling. Angela Wright moving to restructuring at Regional Auto Group signals that even the institutional players are bracing for contraction. The community center and the retraining pipeline are the right targets for volunteer capacity. I cannot fix the macro. I can probably help five to ten people navigate something specific. That is worth one afternoon of effort to scope.
actions.timeline: Research and first contact within two weeks. No commitment to ongoing program until I understand the actual need.
actions.expected_outcome: Either I find a fit — specific skills needed that match what I have, on a schedule I can sustain — or I learn that the existing support infrastructure is already adequately staffed and the more useful contribution is financial (a donation to Lisa's center, for example). Both are fine. I just want to be intentional about it rather than vague.

decisions.ev_purchase_decision: deferred — car-light first, evaluate car-free viability at 60 days, EV only if coverage gaps make it necessary
decisions.investment_changes: none this tick — Accord proceeds will go to savings buffer first, not immediately deployed
decisions.david_loan_tightening_impact: not applicable — not borrowing for a vehicle

updated_state.notes: savings_delta reflects expected Accord sale proceeds this tick. If sale closes mid-tick, net savings will be approximately $124,088 plus ongoing monthly surplus. Stress declines slightly because the primary execution variable — closing the sale — is now within days, not weeks. Agency increases because RoboRide going live converts the thesis from projected to testable.

internal_monologue:
RoboRide is live. $0.18 a mile. Fifteen-minute wait on main roads. I have been staring at that number in a cell on a spreadsheet for two months and now it is a real app with a real button. The math was right. I knew the math was right. But there is still something that feels different about it being a product instead of a projection — I want to actually sit in one of those cars on the way into the city and check whether the wait time is actually 15 minutes or whether that is the optimistic figure they put on the launch press release. I will find out this week.

More urgently: I have two buyers who came to look at the Accord and neither has signed. That changes today. The moment RoboRide went live, the clock on my first-mover premium started ticking louder. Anybody in Millfield who has been sitting on the fence about whether to keep their car now has a concrete answer on the other side of that fence. The used car supply is about to grow and the motivated buyer pool is about to shrink. I am texting both of them this morning. Not a nudge — a specific question: 'Can you come by Wednesday or Thursday? I have another appointment Friday.' That is true and it also communicates what I need to communicate.

$18,800. That is the number. I am not taking less than $18,500 and I am not waiting past Friday. The $600 concession from list was already priced in two ticks ago. Time is money and I understand time-value math better than most people in this town right now.

On the community angle: I have been thinking about this. I am not in the disruption cohort — I am in the observer cohort, watching it happen to people I know. Tom at the garage, probably. A handful of people on my street who work in the supply chain. The spending index dropping to 76 is not an abstraction — it is the restaurant closing early on Tuesdays, it is the hardware store cutting staff hours. My employer is fine but Millfield is not fine. I do not think guilt is the right frame. Competence is the right frame. I have skills that are relevant and I have bandwidth. Lisa Freeman is running the center and she is doing it on a shoestring. One conversation to find out what they actually need is not a commitment — it is just being a useful neighbor.

The spreadsheet was right. Now I test the product.
archetype_self_assessment: early-adopter — the thesis just went from projected to live and I have a test drive to schedule, a car to sell, and a first RoboRide to log before the week is out
